bull_bear.body:
- "Minimal debt in the books" - consolidated non-current borrowings were INR 260 Mn in FY24 and nil in FY25 and FY26; current borrowings INR 273 Mn (FY24), 1,446 Mn (FY25), 2,765 Mn (FY26); AA+ credit rating by CRISIL.
- Returns: "~12% ROCE" as on FY26 end at consolidated level; consolidated ROCE 19.2% (FY24), 16.2% (FY25), 12.0% (FY26) and ROE 14.6%/13.3%/11.6%, with the deck noting "ROCE excluding long term investments is ~12.5% for FY26" consolidated and "~18.3% for FY26" standalone.
- Reinvestment is the visible use of capital: consolidated Capital Work-in-Progress rose from INR 6,255 Mn (FY24) to 12,975 Mn (FY25) to 15,847 Mn (FY26), and PP&E from 29,095 Mn to 37,695 Mn over the same period, funded alongside networth growing from 67,987 Mn (FY24) to 80,990 Mn (FY26).
- New Energy capital is routed through wholly owned subsidiary ARACT (Rs. 1,900 crore infused till date) against the INR 95 Bn Giga Corridor plan.
- Shareholding as on 30th June 2026: Promoter 32.86%, FIIs 17.34%, DIIs 15.30%, Public 34.50%; market cap ~INR 154 Bn+ as on Jun 30, 2026 and shares outstanding 183.0 Mn.

business.body:
- Described as "one of the largest manufacturers of lead-acid batteries in India", with brands 'Amaron', 'PowerZone' and 'Quanta'; the 2023 name change from Amara Raja Batteries Limited "reflects, the broader vision to lead India's Energy Transition, in the Energy & Mobility space by providing comprehensive energy solutions".
- Claims "Leading Automotive Battery Brand", "Largest Exporter of automotive Batteries" and "Strong Brand recall", exporting to 70+ countries; 4 decades of experience and ~12,000 employees.
- In industrial, claims "Pioneers in VRLA batteries in India", "Market Leader in Telecom sector/Largest exporter for VRLA batteries", "Largest Integrated Facility for MVRLA Batteries" and "Market Leader in Telecom and Data Centre Industry".
- Claims first-mover credentials: "First VRLA battery manufacturer", "First AGM battery manufacturer for 2W", and "Developed India's First 21700 Cylindrical Cell (NMC 811)".
- "Rank 1 in S&P Global ESG rating in respective sector in India"; AA+ credit rating by CRISIL; ~1/3rd of shares held by institutional shareholders.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Rename] Renamed from Amara Raja Batteries Limited to Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited in 2023 to signal the shift beyond lead-acid batteries.
- [Group structure] Two named wholly owned subsidiaries carry the strategic build-out: ARACT (Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies) for cells and the 10 GWh BESS plant, and ARCSPL for the lead recycling facility that commenced operations in FY25.
- [Insurance/plant incident] Exceptional income in FY25 of INR 1,111 Mn and in FY26 (net) including INR 1,218 Mn and INR 1,812 Mn relates to insurance claims on the TBD/tubular plant - indicating a plant loss event being recovered through insurance rather than operating performance.
- [Regulation] An INR 476 Mn exceptional expense in Q3 FY26 is attributed to a "change in Labour Code".
- [Distribution] Automotive domestic network slide lists 17, 1,00,000+, 40 and 1500+ against Branches, Distribution Points, Direct Partners and Points of Sale, but the label-to-value binding is not recoverable from this extraction, so the individual counts are not asserted here.

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Amara Raja Energy & Mobility (formerly Amara Raja Batteries) as one of India's largest lead-acid battery makers with leading automotive and telecom/data-centre franchises, now redeploying its cash generation into an INR 95 Bn New Energy "Giga Corridor" in Telangana to lead India's energy transition.

drhp.business: ARE&M manufactures automotive and industrial lead-acid batteries under brands like Amaron and Quanta, and is expanding into new energy through lithium-ion cell and pack manufacturing, EV charging, and battery recycling. The company serves OEMs, aftermarket customers, and infrastructure developers across over 70 countries, with a growing focus on energy storage systems and advanced cell technologies.

drhp.expansion: Amara Raja Circular Solutions Private Limited (ARCS), a wholly owned subsidiary, is establishing a battery recycling facility at Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu. Battery Breaker operations commenced during the year and are in ramp-up. Refining operations, which started in H2 2024, continue to scale up. Phase II refinery expansion is underway with commissioning targeted by 2027. Commissioning of the Crystallizer and De-sulphurisation plant is expected shortly. Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies Private Limited (ARACT) is progressing its lithium-ion cell and battery pack manufacturing capabilities. The Pack Assembly Plant is ramping up towards a targeted annual supply capacity of 1.5 GWh. The Customer Qualification Plant (CQP) with cylindrical and prismatic cell manufacturing lines is in the process of commissioning. Construction at the Amara Raja Giga Corridor in Divitipally, Telangana, progressed substantially, with structural development and procurement of key process equipment advancing. Start of Production (SoP) for lithium-ion cell manufacturing is planned for 2027.

litigation.note: Closure orders received from APPCB in April 2021 for plants at Karakambadi and Nunegundlapalli; interim suspension granted by High Court. APPCB has since sanctioned Consent for Establishment and renewed Consents for Operations for all plants. Company is working with APPCB for closure of legal case.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Established brand leadership in lead-acid batteries with strong distribution network across India and presence in 70+ countries.
- Vertically integrated operations through subsidiary ARCS for battery recycling, securing lead and alloy supply.
- Diversifying into new energy with integrated platform spanning cell manufacturing, pack assembly, energy storage, and EV charging.
- Long-standing technology partnerships and in-house R&D for advanced lead-acid and lithium-ion technologies.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- ARACT is in early-stage ramp-up with net losses, targeting Start of Production by 2027; delays or cost overruns at the Giga Corridor could impact the strategic pivot to New Energy.
- Shift from lead-acid to lithium-ion and advanced chemistries (LFP, NMC) exposes the company to technology risk, customer qualification delays, and potential stranded assets in legacy battery segments.
- ARCS recycling ramp-up (Phase II refinery, de-sulphurisation) is critical for lead and alloy security. Delays in scaling refining or alloy production could disrupt cost and supply-chain resilience.
- Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) under Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, and evolving environmental norms require continuous investment and operational adaptation, especially for recycling and lead operations.
- Automotive and industrial battery segments rely on a concentrated OEM customer base; shifts in OEM procurement strategies or EV adoption rates could materially affect volumes and margins.
- Increasing digitalisation across manufacturing, R&D, and customer interfaces elevates exposure to cyber threats, which could disrupt operations or compromise sensitive data.
- The company is exposed to tightening climate regulations, carbon pricing, and investor expectations. Failure to meet SBTi or GHG reduction targets could lead to reputational damage and higher cost of capital.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthening governance practices through periodic auditor rotation and adoption of an Internal Audit Charter to enhance risk management, internal controls, and governance processes.
- Inculcating a culture of risk management across the organization through extensive training and awareness sessions for employees.
- Conducting CSR activities in education, health, environment, and rural development through Rajanna Foundation and Amara Raja Educational Society.
- Disciplined capital allocation framework balancing investments across established Lead Acid Battery business and emerging New Energy operations, while maintaining a prudent balance sheet and funding flexibility. Capital directed towards manufacturing capacity, recycling infrastructure, cell development capabilities, energy storage solutions and research facilities, with shareholder distributions alongside business investments.
- ARCS is establishing a state-of-the-art battery recycling facility at Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu, with de-sulphurisation technology (first-of-its-kind in India) to improve lead recovery yields, reduce waste, and produce Sodium Sulphate as a by-product.
- ARACT's e+ Energy Labs in Hyderabad is being completed as an integrated research and innovation hub for advanced battery technologies.
- The Company conducts CSR activities through Rajanna Foundation and Amara Raja Educational Society in education, health, environment, and rural development, with impact assessments undertaken for eligible projects.
- The Company has adopted an Internal Audit Charter to strengthen risk management, internal controls, and governance processes.
- The Company has a Whistle Blower Policy/Vigil Mechanism providing a safe and confidential platform for stakeholders to report concerns, including anonymous complaints.
